In this section we are going to learn about backtracking.
Backtracking is a problem solving technique that systematically explore all possible solutions to a
problem.
So if a choice leads to the invalid solution, it backtracks to the previous step and tries to a different
path.
So you can think of this as trying all possibilities step by step and doing choices when they don't
work, and saving time by skipping the invalid options early.
So the simple real life example for backtracking can be choosing an outfit.
So let's say you are picking an outfit from the following items.
You have three shirts in color of red, blue and white, and you have two pants in color of black and
blue.
And you have two shoes, sneakers and boots, which is white and black.
Now you want to find all possible stylish combinations, so backtracking will work like this.
First, let's say you are selecting the red shirt.
Then we are going to pair it with the next pant.
So the pant is going to be blue.
So let's say in this case you don't like this.
So you are going to eliminate this option.
So you will go to back and select the next pant.
So the next pant is black.
So we see that they pair with each other.
So we can continue to select the boot.
So in this case this is going to be our one option.
Now if you are looking for all possible options we are going to continue back and select the next shirt.
Now the next t shirt is blue.
So we are going to pair it with blue.
So let's say we don't like it.
So we are going to continue back and select the next pant.
So the next pant is going to be black pant.
